objective: Bring the independent BTS-to-DR24 spatial-recovery and Lightcurves-availability tooling onto current main as a bounded, manual-only research workflow. Preserve raw provenance and keep all outputs separate from the production selector.
previous_knowledge_consumed: The 100-object BTS spatial-recovery pilot recovered 773 DR24 OIDs within a 5-arcsecond candidate-generation radius and recorded filter and field/CCD/quadrant provenance.
The indexed Lightcurves HATS query found 714/773 recovered OIDs and 59 missing rows; row availability does not prove photometry quality.
A separate four-OID nested-payload probe retrieved 626 epoch rows and preserves HMJD, native magnitude, magerr, clrcoeff, catflags, and partition metadata.
A ZTF OID is not a universal astrophysical identity; filter/field/quadrant context must be preserved.
CPVS exact-reconstruction is deferred research and is not a dependency for this independent BTS/DR24 workstream.

baseline.description: Adds independent, standalone research scripts, deterministic fixture tests, a report, and a manual-only bounded workflow. No application runtime, model, feature schema, taxonomy, benchmark, or acceptance criteria change.

reproducibility.before: The 100-target BTS-to-DR24 recovery results existed as recorded workflow artifacts but the complete acquisition/query/audit tooling was not registered on current main.
reproducibility.after: The repository contains reproducible BTS snapshot acquisition, DR24 spatial query, OID multiplicity audit, indexed Lightcurves availability query, and deterministic tests.

correctness.before: The recovery pilot scripts were not available in current main for rerun.
correctness.after: The tools retain all candidate OIDs, recompute angular separation, preserve available partition metadata, and report ambiguity/multiplicity without asserting physical identity.

reliability.reason: The new manual-only workflow must be executed on current main before operational repeatability is measured.

measurement.trade_off: The live source-backed workflow is manual-only and capped at 100 BTS targets per run to control query load. Routine CI runs fixtures only.

evidence: Run deterministic fixture tests through ordinary CI.
Validate the lifecycle record and all documentation/code formatting.
Confirm the live BTS/DR24 workflow is workflow_dispatch-only, bounded to 1–100 targets, and has contents:read permissions.
No full-catalog scan, production normalization, model inference, or release is part of this PR.

root_causes: The previous recovery tooling branch was based on an older main revision and its workflow included push and pull_request triggers for source-backed acquisition.
The source-backed pilot needed to be retained as a reproducible research tool without making live external queries part of routine CI or every main push.

findings: BTS coordinates can generate DR24 candidate associations but do not prove physical identity.
Filter, field, CCD, quadrant, and OID provenance must be retained when interpreting multiplicity.
The 5-arcsecond radius is candidate generation only; it is not an accepted identity threshold.
Objects Table OID availability and Lightcurves row availability are distinct.
Raw payload retrieval, photometry normalization, quality policy, and model performance are separate validation stages.

open_blockers: Current-head CI and deterministic fixture tests must pass.
A manual source-backed run on current main is required to verify repeatability.
The scripts do not implement the production DR24 observation adapter or cross-OID physical identity.

knowledge_carried_forward: Keep the workflow manual-only and bounded to 100 BTS targets per run.
Preserve raw and normalized data as separate artifacts with hashes.
Do not label multiple OIDs as false positives without partition and identity evidence.
Do not treat row availability as photometry quality.
Do not connect this research tooling to production inference until Issue #253 acceptance criteria pass.
